headline: Adobe acquires Indian marketing intelligence startup Rilo
summary: Adobe has acquired Rilo, a startup focused on automating marketing workflows, to bolster its AI-powered marketing tools for enterprise clients.
details: Adobe has acquired India-based marketing intelligence startup Rilo, confirming a deal that involves licensing and team acquisition. This marks Adobe's second acquisition from India, following the purchase of video platform Rephrase.ai in 2023. The financial terms of the deal were not disclosed.

Rilo's technology focuses on automating marketing workflows, a crucial area as companies increasingly leverage AI for campaign creation, deployment, and tracking. The startup's tools can also extract action items from meetings and enhance brand visibility across platforms like ChatGPT and Gemini.

Founded in 2025 by IIT batchmates Georgi Boby and Dhruv Jaglan, Rilo had previously raised $1 million from investors including PeakXV and Day Zero Ventures. Adobe will integrate Rilo's intellectual property and its six-member team.

Rilo's platform allowed go-to-market teams to build custom workflows for tasks such as competitor intelligence, content repurposing, and sales call analysis. Post-acquisition, Rilo will cease operations and will no longer be available to its existing customers.

This acquisition strengthens Adobe's position in the competitive marketing technology landscape, where rivals like Canva are also expanding their portfolios and major tech players like Amazon, Google, and Meta are developing their own AI-driven marketing solutions.

Rilo's platform allowed go-to-market teams to build custom workflows for tasks such as competitor intelligence, content repurposing, and sales call analysis. Post-acquisition, Rilo will cease operations and will no longer be available to its existing customers.

This acquisition strengthens Adobe's position in the competitive marketing technology landscape, where rivals like Canva are also expanding their portfolios and major tech players like Amazon, Google, and Meta are developing their own AI-driven marketing solutions.
